variable.name: Air temperature
variable.plain: Average air temperature 2 metres above the ground.

alibi.headline: No documented change of instrument or model input inside this record.

el_nino.headline: Still there with El Niño removed: +0.339 °C/decade (was +0.333).
el_nino.how_linked: This place hardly follows El Niño (r = +0.09, 0-month delay).
el_nino.method: Foster & Rahmstorf (2011): regression on trend + ENSO index at the best-fitting lag

climate_modes.headline: Still there with North Atlantic Oscillation removed: +0.363 °C/decade (was +0.333).
climate_modes.strongest: Strongest link: North Atlantic Oscillation (r = +0.36; in Dec–Feb r = +0.53).

links.name: Pacific Decadal Oscillation
links.index: NOAA NCEI ERSST v5 PDO index

climate_modes.method: Correlation of detrended anomalies with each index (best lag 0–3 months; Dec–Feb and Jun–Aug also separately); linked modes (|r| ≥ 0.2 overall, or ≥ 0.35 in Dec–Feb or Jun–Aug) fitted together with the trend and removed (Foster & Rahmstorf 2011).

leave_one_out.headline: No single year carries it: removing any one year keeps it proven (weakest without 1987, p = 6.1e-09).

walk_forward.headline: Confirmed: found in 1981–2002 and found again, the same way, in 2003–2025.

all_windows.headline: Not cherry-picked: 468 of 496 possible start/end choices (94%) show it rising. Replaying the record from 1981, the evidence became strong by 1999 and has stayed strong every year since.
all_windows.method: Yue–Wang modified Mann–Kendall on yearly means, every window of 15 years or more

decades.headline: No proven speed-up or slow-down (p = 0.81). Last 15 years: +0.791 °C/decade; whole record: +0.345.

extremes.headline: The last 10 years averaged +1.28 °C compared with the first 10 (p = 7e-05). 3 of the 3 highest years are in the last 10.

resolution.label: resolved
resolution.headline: 4 NASA grid cells (~50 km each) inside this area: a regional picture.

seasons.headline: 10 of 12 months show a proven change (Feb, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec). Biggest change: Feb (+0.567 °C/decade).
seasons.method: Each calendar month tested alone (Yue–Wang Mann–Kendall + Sen), Benjamini–Hochberg across the 12; seasonal Kendall (Hirsch et al. 1982) and the correlated-seasons version (Hirsch & Slack 1984).

change_point.headline: Most change happened after about 2002, but a steady trend describes it as well or better than a sudden jump: read this as gradual change, not one event (Pettitt p = 0.00057).
change_point.method: Pettitt (1979) test on yearly anomalies; step vs steady trend compared with BIC (difference > 2).

could_overturn: MERRA-2 is a reanalysis (a weather model steered by observations), not a thermometer: an independent witness agreeing makes the case much stronger.

score.headline: Passed 5 of 5 cross-examination checks (instrument, El Niño, one year, two halves, dates).
checks: instrument alibi: survives or no known change
first half confirmed or continued in the second
no start/end years give a proven opposite trend
score.rule_note: These five pass rules were written on Sat 14 Nov (~20:15) while building this check, after the main Lincolnshire result was already known: they were not pre-registered. Each failure is listed, so read the individual checks, not just the count.
